text:
elaine (Docs): Hey folks, opened a PR to add autoscaling policy examples for Dedicated pools. Needs review for correctness and a quick link fix (pricing -> dedicated-reserved). PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/1312

rui (Infra): nice. Which metric did you use in the examples? queue_depth or p50_latency?

elaine (Docs): both — one example for latency-based scaling, one for queue-depth scaling. Trying to be explicit about cooldown and max burst.

mike (SRE): for Dedicated we usually recommend p95 latency as the trigger, not p50. p95 avoids oscillation from transient spikes. Also set cooldown to >= 60s.

elaine (Docs): thanks, changed p50 -> p95 and cooldown to 60s. Added sample HCL for autoscale_policy. Can you eyeball the resource names?

rui (Infra): resource names look good but change attribute name from "scale_step" to "scale_increment" to match the provider. Example tweak: 

```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "ml-pool" {
  name        = "ml-pool"
  gpu_type    = "h100-80gb"
  min_capacity = 4
  max_capacity = 32
}

resource "redwood_dedicated_autoscale" "ml-autoscale" {
  pool_id          = redwood_dedicated_pool.ml-pool.id
  metric           = "p95_latency_ms"
  threshold        = 250
  scale_increment  = 4
  cooldown_seconds = 60
  max_burst        = 8
}
```

elaine (Docs): swapped to scale_increment. Also added a Python SDK snippet for creating the policy.

zoe (Product): include a short callout about billing: burst minutes are pro-rated by minute; mention that sustained autoscale beyond committed capacity may affect committed spend forecasts.

elaine (Docs): added a billing callout. Wording: "Burst minutes above committed throughput are pro-rated and will appear in the usage invoice; customers on committed contracts may see adjustments to committed utilization calculations." ok?

ben (Support): good. Also there was a dead link in the migration checklist to the Dedicated pricing page (old path /pricing/dedicated). I replaced it with /pricing/dedicated-reserved and updated the anchor text.

elaine (Docs): great catch, thanks. CI error earlier flagged a bad anchor in the SLO table. Fixed the heading slug.

mike (SRE): another ops note: clarify isolation semantics — Dedicated provides tenant-isolated GPU allocation and per-tenant KV caches; however, some control-plane logs and aggregated metrics are shared for platform observability. Add a security pointer to KMS scope for customer keys.

elaine (Docs): added: "Network isolation: VPC peering or private link is required for Private deployments; Dedicated supports customer VPC peering for egress control. Customer KMS keys may be scoped per-tenant for model artifacts and audit logs."

rui (Infra): tiny nit on the HCL: kms_key should be kms_key_arn. Also add example for preemptible fallback policy (for non-guaranteed capacity).

elaine (Docs): updated kms_key_arn and added a short preemptible fallback paragraph: 

"If a pool uses preemptible capacity for cost savings, we recommend a fallback policy that routes to a compatible non-preemptible pool or reduces batch sizes. Preemptible fallback may increase tail latency; see SLO adjustments below."

zoe (Product): add a short table-row in the SLA matrix: "Dedicated - burst fallback: latency SLOs may be relaxed by up to 30% during preemptible fallback; billing is pro-rated."

elaine (Docs): added row and referenced the pricing page. Anything else?

ben (Support): approve customer-facing wording. Maybe add a short migration checklist item: "Verify KMS access and VPC peering before cutover."

elaine (Docs): added migration checklist item. CI bot: docs build queued.

ci-bot: build status - docs CI passed: https://ci.internal/builds/4903 :white_check_mark:

elaine (Docs): awesome, merging now and will ping #customer-success with the migration link. Thanks all! :party_popper:
